title and abstract.summary: This study investigated how land-use conversion from forest to rubber plantation impacts the distribution of functional traits and trait space in foraging ant assemblages in tropical Thailand by integrating both physiological and morphological traits.

introduction.summary: The study investigated how land-use transformation (from forest to rubber plantation) shapes foraging ant assemblages by examining the influence of thermal constraints and habitat simplification on the functional traits of these ant assemblages.

methods.summary: The study measured the critical thermal maximum ($ ext{CT}_{ ext{max}}$) and morphological traits of two ant species collected from different habitats.
